_doc: RFC_029 §10.15 — the `?` OPTIONAL-EXPLICIT marker on ExtractActionInputs' step-config surface (council REVISE round 1, bug_historian's gating objection). A `?` wire resolves its declared path OR LEAVES THE FIELD ABSENT, deliberately with no error, no log and no row: absence is the contract. Nothing at runtime can tell an intended absence from a mistyped path, so the guard is offline and fleet-wide — `config-key-audit --optional-explicit-wires` lists every live `?` wire and exits 1 on any that is not acknowledged here. An entry records that a human READ THE DOWNSTREAM CODE of the consuming action and confirmed it treats an absent field as a safe no-op, rather than as an empty string or zero it will render or persist. `downstream` is not optional in spirit: an entry with an empty statement is ignored (and warned about), because an ack that says nothing about what was checked is precisely the hollow ack the objection named. Key shape is `<action>.<field>` — keyed on the ACTION, because coping-with-absence is a property of the code that consumes the field, not of which workflow wired it. Sibling file and precedent: optional_key_budget_acks.json (RFC_022).
_no_entries_yet: The marker shipped with ZERO adopters (v1.0.1321, live 2026-08-20; census 2026-08-21: 0 `?` keys on this surface, 77 on the input_mapping surface which this audit deliberately does not report). The first adopter adds the first entry here in the same commit as its migration.
